easy.def: The feeling you get when you are scared.
examples: I have a fear of spiders.
She felt fear in the dark.
His fear went away.

more.def: The unpleasant feeling you get when you think something bad may happen.
examples: She felt fear when the lights went out.
He has a fear of high places.
Her fear of dogs grew smaller each day.

easy.def: To be afraid of something.
examples: I fear spiders.
She fears the dark.
They fear the storm.

more.def: To be afraid of something because you think it may hurt you.
examples: Many people fear thunder.
He feared that the ice might crack.
Some animals fear fire.

easy.def: Not afraid of anything.
examples: The fearless girl jumped.
He is fearless in the water.
A fearless dog barked.

more.def: Not afraid, even when something is hard or dangerous.
examples: The fearless explorer walked into the dark cave with just a flashlight.
She was fearless on the high diving board.
The fearless little dog barked at the big gate.

easy.def: A big, special meal.
examples: We had a feast.
The feast was big.
The feast had many foods.

more.def: A large, special meal with lots of good food.
examples: We had a feast on Thanksgiving.
The table was full of food for the feast.
The king held a feast for the whole town.

easy.def: Something hard that takes skill or courage.
examples: Climbing the mountain was a feat.
That was a great feat.
He did an amazing feat.

more.def: An act that shows great skill, strength or courage, especially one that is hard to do.
examples: Climbing to the top of the mountain in one day was an amazing feat.
Building a boat from scraps was quite a feat for the young inventors.
The gymnast's flip in the air was a feat of balance and strength.

easy.def: A light, soft part that covers a bird.
examples: A bird lost a feather.
The feather is soft.
I found a blue feather.

more.def: One of the soft, light parts that cover a bird's body.
examples: I found a blue feather on the path.
Birds use their feathers to fly and to stay warm.
The pillow was filled with soft feathers.

related.def: Light and soft like a feather.

easy.def: An important part of something.
examples: The pool is a feature of the hotel.
A big feature of the car is its roof.
Her smile is her best feature.

more.def: An important or noticeable part of something.
examples: A big pool is a feature of the hotel.
A big window is the best feature of this room.
The camera has many features.

easy.def: The second month of the year.
examples: My birthday is in February.
We make snowmen in February.
February is cold here.

more.def: The second month of the year, which has 28 days, or 29 in a leap year.
examples: February is the shortest month of the year.
Every four years, February has an extra day.
Snow often covers the ground in February.

easy.def: Having to do with the national government.
examples: The federal government makes laws.
A federal law.
The federal building is big.

more.def: Having to do with the government that rules a whole country made of states.
examples: The federal government makes national laws.
The federal building is downtown.
Our country has federal and state laws.

easy.def: Money you pay to do something.
examples: There is a fee to enter the park.
The fee is five dollars.
We paid a fee.

more.def: An amount of money that you pay to get into a place or use something.
examples: There is a small fee to enter the museum.
The swimming lesson fee is ten dollars.
We paid a fee at the gate.

easy.def: To give food to a person or animal.
examples: I feed the cat.
Mom fed the baby.
We feed the ducks.

more.def: To give food to a person or animal so that it can live and grow.
examples: We feed the chickens every morning.
She fed the baby with a spoon.
Farmers feed the cows hay in winter.

easy.def: Food for farm animals.
examples: The horse eats feed.
We bought feed for the chickens.
The cows like their feed.

more.def: Food given to farm animals, such as hay or grain.
examples: The farmer bought a bag of feed for the chickens.
Cattle feed is stored in the barn.
The horse ate its feed.

easy.def: To notice something inside you, like being happy or cold.
examples: I feel happy.
She feels cold.
We felt tired.

more.def: To have a certain emotion or sense in your body or mind.
examples: I feel proud when I finish a hard puzzle.
He felt sick after riding the spinning ride.
Do you feel warm enough in that jacket?

easy.def: To touch something to learn about it.
examples: Feel the soft fur.
She felt the cold ice.
I feel the wind.

more.def: To touch something with your hands to learn what it is like.
examples: Feel how smooth this stone is.
He felt the bread to see if it was still warm.
The nurse felt my forehead to check for a fever.

easy.def: What you feel inside, like being happy or sad.
examples: Joy is a feeling.
I have a good feeling.
She hid her feeling.

more.def: An emotion such as happiness, fear, or anger that you feel inside.
examples: Happiness is a warm feeling that makes you smile.
He had a nervous feeling before the big test.
It is okay to talk about your feelings.

easy.def: A man or boy.
examples: A friendly fellow helped us.
That fellow is my uncle.
He is a funny fellow.

more.def: A man or boy, in a casual way.
examples: He is a kind old fellow who feeds the birds.
That fellow over there is my uncle.
A tall fellow carried the box.

easy.def: In the same group.
examples: My fellow classmates cheered.
She helped her fellow campers.
A fellow traveler gave me a seat.

more.def: Belonging to the same group or sharing the same situation as you.
examples: She waved to her fellow students.
The soldiers helped their fellow soldier.
A fellow passenger shared an umbrella.

easy.def: Friendly time spent with a group.
examples: We enjoy the fellowship at the club.
The picnic was full of fellowship.
Fellowship makes us feel warm.

more.def: A friendly feeling among people who share the same interests, or a group of people who join together for a goal.
examples: The scouts enjoyed the fellowship of singing around the campfire.
The hikers felt a sense of fellowship as they shared snacks at the top.
The book club is a fellowship of people who love adventure stories.

easy.def: A soft, thick cloth.
examples: I made a hat out of felt.
The felt is soft.
She cut a star from felt.

more.def: A soft, thick cloth made by pressing wool or other fibers together.
examples: She cut a green leaf shape out of felt.
The bottom of the chair has a piece of felt.
He glued felt to the back of the pin.

easy.def: Being the kind that can lay eggs or have babies.
examples: A female cat.
The female bird laid eggs.
A female horse.

more.def: Belonging to the group of people or animals that can have babies or lay eggs.
examples: A female cat can have kittens.
The female bird sat on the nest.
A female horse is called a mare.

easy.def: A woman, girl or she-animal.
examples: The female has spots.
A female was in the cage.
The female is smaller.

more.def: A woman, a girl or an animal that is able to have babies.
examples: The female of the species is smaller.
Two females stayed with the cubs.
The female guards the nest.

easy.def: Of or like girls and women.
examples: Feminine means like a woman.
She is a feminine name.
The word is feminine in French.

more.def: Having to do with women or girls, or usually thought of as belonging to them.
examples: Maria is a feminine name in many countries.
In French, the word for a table is a feminine word.
The shop sold clothes in both masculine and feminine styles.

easy.def: A wall made of posts and boards or wire around an area.
examples: We painted the fence.
The fence keeps the dog in.
A fence is around the yard.

more.def: A wall of wood or wire that goes around a place to keep things in or out.
examples: A white fence stood around the yard.
The fence keeps the horses in the field.
The cat jumped over the fence.

easy.def: The part of a car or bike over the wheel.
examples: The car has a dent in its fender.
The bike fender is red.
Mud was on the fender.

more.def: The curved part of a car, bicycle or other vehicle that sits over the wheel and keeps mud and water from splashing up.
examples: The truck had a dent in the front fender after it scraped the gate.
A fender on a bicycle keeps mud from splashing up on your back.
Rain dripped from the fender onto the road.

easy.def: A green plant with feathery leaves and no flowers.
examples: The fern is green.
A fern grows in the shade.
We have a fern.

more.def: A green plant with feathery leaves that grows in damp, shady places and has no flowers.
examples: A fern grows in the shade of the tree.
The fern has feathery green leaves.
We put a fern in a pot on the porch.

easy.def: A boat that carries people and cars across water.
examples: We took the ferry.
The ferry crossed the bay.
The ferry has cars.

more.def: A boat that carries people and vehicles back and forth across a stretch of water.
examples: We took the ferry to the island.
The ferry crossed the bay in twenty minutes.
Cars drove onto the ferry.

easy.def: A big party for a special day.
examples: We ate treats at the festival.
There was music at the festival.
We go to the fall festival.

more.def: A special time when people celebrate with events, food, or music.
examples: The town holds a kite festival every spring.
The film festival shows movies from around the world.
Lanterns lit up the streets during the festival.

easy.def: To go and bring something back.
examples: The dog will fetch the ball.
Fetch me my shoes.
She fetched a glass of water.

more.def: To go to get something and bring it back.
examples: The dog fetched the stick and dropped it at my feet.
Please fetch me a glass of water.
She fetched her coat from the hall.

easy.def: Being hotter than normal because you are sick.
examples: I have a fever.
The nurse took my temperature to check for a fever.
A fever makes you feel hot.

more.def: A higher body temperature than normal, usually a sign that you are sick.
examples: The nurse checked if I had a fever.
He stayed home with a fever and a cough.
A fever makes you feel hot and tired.

easy.def: Not many.
examples: I have a few toys.
Few kids came.
There are few cookies.

more.def: A small number of things or people.
examples: Only a few clouds floated in the blue sky.
A few of my friends came to the park.
I will be back in a few minutes.
